before: A table of contents row and a PAGEREF result named the page of a heading's first fragment, which holds only a leading page break. New _Toc bookmarks started before that break.
after: They name the page where the heading text is painted. New _Toc bookmarks start after leading page and column breaks. Shared operations and their fields are unchanged.
reason: Peers replicate the resulting tree, not the replaceTocResult or rewriteTocPageNumbers operations, so the bookmark position a peer writes reaches every peer as ordinary content. An older peer that refreshes writes its own page number text, which every peer applies normally.
